text: To apply a parallelogram equal to a given triangle to a given straight-line in a given rectilinear angle. Let $AB$ be the given straight-line,  $C$ the given triangle, and $D$ the given rectilinear angle. So it is required to apply a parallelogram equal to the given triangle $C$ to the given straight-line $AB$ in an angle equal to (angle) $D$.
Let the parallelogram $BEFG$, equal to the triangle $C$, have been constructed in the angle $EBG$, which is equal to $D$ [Prop.~1.42].
And let it have been placed so that $BE$ is straight-on to $AB$.
And let $FG$ have been drawn through to $H$,
and let $AH$ have been drawn through A parallel to either of $BG$ or $EF$ [Prop.~1.31],
and let $HB$ have been joined.
And since the straight-line $HF$ falls across the parallels $AH$ and $EF$, the (sum of the) angles $AHF$ and $HFE$ is thus equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.29].
assertion: the sum of angles AHF and HFE equals two right-angles

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the straight-line $HF$ falls across the parallels $AH$ and $EF$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (sum of the) angles $AHF$ and $HFE$ is thus equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, (the sum of) $BHG$ and $GFE$ is less than two right-angles.
assertion: the sum of angles BHG and GFE is less than two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $BHG$ and $GFE$ is less than two right-angles

text: And (straight-lines) produced to infinity from (internal angles whose sum is) less than two right-angles meet together [Post.~5].
assertion: straight-lines from angles summing to less than two right-angles meet when produced

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (straight-lines) produced to infinity from (internal angles whose sum is) less than two right-angles meet together

text: Thus, being produced, $HB$ and $FE$ will meet together.
assertion: HB and FE, when produced, meet

text: Let them have been produced, and let them meet together at $K$.
And let $KL$ have been drawn through point $K$ parallel to either of $EA$ or $FH$ [Prop.~1.31].
And let $HA$ and $GB$ have been produced to points $L$ and $M$ (respectively).
Thus, $HLKF$ is a parallelogram,
and $HK$ its diagonal.
assertion: HK is the diagonal of HLKF

text: And $AG$ and $ME$ (are) parallelograms,
and $LB$ and $BF$ the so-called complements, about $HK$.
assertion: LB and BF are the complements about HK

text: Thus, $LB$ is equal to $BF$ [Prop.~1.43].
But, $BF$ is equal to triangle $C$.
Thus, $LB$ is also equal to $C$.
Also, since angle $GBE$ is equal to $ABM$ [Prop.~1.15], but $GBE$ is equal to $D$, $ABM$ is thus also equal to angle $D$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $ABM$ is thus also equal to angle $D$

text: Thus, the parallelogram $LB$, equal to the given triangle $C$, has been applied to the given straight-line $AB$ in the angle $ABM$, which is equal to $D$. (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
